statement.p: In this problem we use the change of variables x=5 s + t, y = s - 3 t to compute the integral \int_R (x+y)\,dA, where R is the parallelogram with vertices (x,y)=(0,0), (5,1), (7,-5), and (2,-6).
First find the magnitude of the Jacobian, \left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right| = .

static.solution:
\begin{array}{ccc} x \amp = \amp 5 s + t\\ y \amp = \amp s - 3 t, \end{array} we have \left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right| = \left|\begin{array}{cc} \frac{\partial x}{\partial s} \amp \frac{\partial x}{\partial t}\\ \frac{\partial y}{\partial s} \amp \frac{\partial y}{\partial t} \end{array}\right| =\left|\begin{array}{cc} 5 \amp 1 \\ 1 \amp -3 \end{array}\right| = |-16|, hence \left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right| = 16. We therefore get \int_R (x+y) \,dA = \int_{T} ((5 s + t) + (s - 3 t)) \left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(s,t)}\right|dsdt = \int_{T}(6s-2t)(16)\,ds\,dt=\int_{T} (16\mathopen{}\left(6s-2t\right))\,ds\,dt, where T is the region in the st-plane corresponding to R.
Now, we need to find T.
Because \begin{array}{ccc} x \amp = \amp 5 s+ t \\ y \amp = \amp s - 3 t \end{array} we can use the boundaries of the region R to find the boundaries of T. Using the four vertices of the parallelogram R, we the edges y = \frac1{5}\,x, y = -3\,x, y = \frac{1}{5}\,(x-2) - 6 and y = -3(x - 5) + 1. So, from the above transformation, the boundaries are t = 0, s = 0, t = 2 and s = 1. Therefore \int_R(x+y)\,dA = \int_{0}^{2} \int_{0}^{1}\, 16\mathopen{}\left(6s-2t\right) \,ds\,dt = 32. (Alternately, we could of course also write the integral as \int_{2}^{0} \int_{1}^{0}\, 16\mathopen{}\left(6s-2t\right) \,ds\,dt.)
